title: Adjectives: agreement and position
description: Four-form and two-form adjectives, invariable colours, and where adjectives go.
objectives: Make adjectives agree in gender and number with their noun.
Distinguish -o adjectives (four forms) from -e adjectives (two forms).
Place adjectives correctly, usually after the noun.

blocks.title: Agreement
blocks.text: An adjective takes the gender and number of the noun it describes: *il gatto nero, la gatta nera, i gatti neri, le gatte nere*.
Invariable colour adjectives include *blu, rosa, viola*: *le farfalle rosa* (the pink butterflies).

blocks.title: Mixed groups take the masculine plural
blocks.text: One adjective describing a masculine and a feminine noun together is masculine plural: *Il gatto e la volpe sono stanchi.*

blocks.title: -co/-go adjectives follow the noun pattern
blocks.text: *bianco → bianchi, bianche*; *lungo → lunghi, lunghe*. But stress-early adjectives take -ci: *simpatico → simpatici* (feminine always -che: *simpatiche*).

blocks.title: Most adjectives follow the noun
blocks.text: Colours, shapes, nationalities and most descriptive adjectives come after the noun: *un gatto nero, una canzone italiana, un fiume lungo*.

blocks.title: Some common adjectives often precede
blocks.text: *bello, buono, brutto, grande, piccolo, nuovo, vecchio, giovane, lungo* often come before the noun, especially in a subjective or emotional sense: *una bella giornata, un piccolo orso*.

examples.note: piccolo before the noun: affectionate, storybook tone.

exercises.explanation: Feminine singular of an -o adjective: rossa.
notte is feminine; plural notti; feminine plural adjective: fredde.

mistakes.message: notti ends in -i but is feminine (la notte), so the adjective is feminine plural: fredde.

exercises.explanation: -e adjectives have one plural form for both genders: felici.
-co adjectives keep the hard sound: bianchi, bianche.

exercises.prompt: What does *un grande uomo* usually mean?
exercises.explanation: Before the noun grande tends to mean 'great'; after it, 'big': un uomo grande.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'The black cat sleeps.'

summary: Adjectives agree with the noun in gender and number.
-o adjectives: -o, -a, -i, -e. -e adjectives: -e, -i. Some colours are invariable.
Most adjectives follow the noun; a few common ones often precede it, sometimes with a different meaning.

title: Demonstratives and possessives
description: questo and quello; mio, tuo, suo, nostro, vostro, loro — with and without the article.
objectives: Use questo and quello in all their forms.
Use possessives with the definite article.
Know when family nouns drop the article.

blocks.text: *questo* behaves like an ordinary -o adjective: *questo libro, questa casa, questi libri, queste case*. Before a vowel in the singular it may elide: *quest'albero*.

blocks.title: quello before a noun copies the definite article
blocks.text: Take the article the noun would have and attach it to *que-*: il → *quel*, lo → *quello*, l' → *quell'*, la → *quella*, i → *quei*, gli → *quegli*, le → *quelle*.

blocks.title: Agreement with the thing possessed
blocks.text: The possessive agrees with the noun it accompanies, not with the owner: *il suo libro* = his book or her book; *la sua casa* = his house or her house.

blocks.title: The article is normally used
blocks.text: Possessives are normally preceded by the definite article: *il mio cane, la nostra casa*.

blocks.title: Singular family nouns
blocks.text: With a **singular**, unmodified family noun the article is dropped: *mio padre, mia sorella, tuo fratello*. It returns in the plural (*i miei fratelli*), with *loro* (*il loro padre*), with an adjective (*la mia sorella piccola*), and usually with affectionate forms (*la mia mamma, il mio papà*).

examples.it: I miei nonni abitano al mare.
examples.en: My grandparents live by the sea.
Marco is looking for his ball.
examples.note: sua agrees with palla (feminine), not with Marco.

exercises.explanation: alberi takes gli, so quello becomes quegli.

exercises.prompt: Sara and her book: Sara legge ___ libro.
exercises.explanation: libro is masculine, so il suo — Sara's gender does not matter.

mistakes.message: The possessive agrees with libro (masculine), not with Sara: il suo libro.

exercises.explanation: Singular family noun without adjective: no article.
loro is invariable and always takes the article.

exercises.prompt: Translate: My grandparents live by the sea.
exercises.answer: I miei nonni abitano al mare.
accept: I miei nonni vivono al mare.
exercises.explanation: Plural family noun: the article is used (i miei nonni). al mare = by the sea / at the seaside.

summary: questo: -o, -a, -i, -e. quello before a noun copies the article: quel, quello, quell', quella, quei, quegli, quelle.
Possessives agree with the thing possessed and normally take the article.
No article with a singular unmodified family noun (mia madre); loro always takes the article.

title: bello and buono; comparing things
description: The special forms of bello and buono before nouns, and elementary comparatives.
objectives: Use bel, bello, bell', bei, begli and buon before nouns.
Make comparisons with più … di, meno … di and come.
Know the irregular comparatives migliore and peggiore.

sections.heading: bello and buono before a noun

blocks.title: bello copies the definite article
blocks.text: Like *quello*, *bello* before a noun takes the form of the article: *bel* (il), *bello* (lo), *bell'* (l'), *bella* (la), *bei* (i), *begli* (gli), *belle* (le). After the noun or after *essere* it is a regular -o adjective: *Il fiore è bello. I fiori sono belli.*

blocks.title: buono copies the indefinite article
blocks.text: In the singular before a noun: *buon* (un), *buono* (uno), *buona* (una), *buon'* (un'): *buon giorno, buono zucchero, buona notte, buon'idea*. Plurals are regular: *buoni, buone*.

blocks.caption: Comparing two things
rows: La lepre è più veloce della tartaruga.
La tartaruga è meno veloce della lepre.
Luca è alto come suo padre.

blocks.title: di combines with the article
blocks.text: *di* + article contracts: *della tartaruga, del cane, dei gatti*. Before a name or pronoun there is no article: *più alto di Marco, più alta di me*.

blocks.title: di or che?
blocks.text: Use *di* when two different people or things are compared for the same quality, and the second term is a noun, name or pronoun: *Marco è più alto di Luca. Sei più brava di me.* Use *che* in all the other cases: two qualities of the same thing (*È più bello che utile*), two verbs (*Leggere è più facile che scrivere*), two quantities (*Ho più libri che quaderni*), two terms introduced by a preposition (*Fa più caldo a Roma che a Milano*), and two adverbs (*Meglio tardi che mai*).

blocks.title: Comparing with a clause
blocks.text: When the second term is a whole clause, use *di quanto* or *di quello che*: *È più difficile di quanto pensassi / di quello che pensavo.* After *di quanto* the congiuntivo is common in careful style; the indicativo is also used.

blocks.title: migliore and peggiore
blocks.text: *buono* has the comparative *migliore* (better), *cattivo* has *peggiore* (worse). *più buono* and *più cattivo* are also correct, especially about taste and character. The adverbs are *meglio* (better) and *peggio* (worse).

examples.it: La lepre è più veloce della tartaruga.
examples.en: The hare is faster than the tortoise.

examples.it: Il gatto è meno grande del cane.
examples.en: The cat is smaller (less big) than the dog.

examples.it: Questa torta è migliore di quella.
examples.en: This cake is better than that one.

exercises.explanation: After essere bello is a regular adjective: belli. bei/begli are only for before a noun.

exercises.prompt: Translate: Luca is as tall as his father.
exercises.answer: Luca è alto come suo padre.
accept: Luca è così alto come suo padre.
Luca è alto quanto suo padre.
Luca è tanto alto quanto suo padre.
exercises.explanation: (così) … come or (tanto) … quanto; suo padre without article.

exercises.prompt: Which word means 'better' as an adjective (a better cake)?
exercises.explanation: migliore is the adjective (una torta migliore); meglio is the adverb (sto meglio).

summary: bello before a noun: bel, bello, bell', bella, bei, begli, belle (like the definite article).
buono before a singular noun: buon, buono, buona, buon' (like the indefinite article).
più / meno + adjective + di (+ article); (così) … come for equality.
